source.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) transfer across base and finetuned language models?
source.authors: Taras Kutsyk; Tommaso Mencattini; Ciprian Florea

record.tranche_reason: It measures activation similarity and tests whether a base-model SAE transfers to related finetuned models, a different operationalization of representational alignment. It does not test convergence with scale or across independently trained, different-modality models.
record.gate_note: The study compares two base/finetune pairs, using a base-trained SAE on each pair and the SAE's training dataset. It reports activation similarity, SAE reconstruction and feature-similarity results. It does not test model scaling, independent seeds, or vision-language alignment. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study applies one base-trained SAE to a base model and its own full finetune: Gemma-2b vs. Gemma-2b-it-python-codes, and Mistral-7B vs. MetaMath-Mistral-7B. It also compares their residual activations. Each pair shares initialization and pretraining, so this measures how much representations persist under finetuning. It does not measure convergence between independently trained models, seeds, architectures or modalities. No map between separate models' representations is learned (the SAE is reused as-is). No features are recovered independently in each model and then matched. It has no scale axis. The universality method from Towards Monosemanticity is borrowed as a proxy for features persisting after finetuning, not to test universality across models. These findings are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that transfer depends on the model and finetune (poor for Gemma-2b python-codes, good for Mistral MetaMath). They say activation similarity or weight deviation may predict transfer, and that some Gemma features might persist, which is tentative.
record.recipe_differences: Tests reuse of a base-trained SAE and measure activation and feature similarity, rather than testing the original sources' claims about convergence with scale, seeds, or cross-modal models.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer results differ between the two model/finetune pairs and across operational measures. The post uses only each SAE's original training dataset; it does not vary datasets or similarity settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Base-trained SAEs degrade badly on the Gemma-2b python finetune and hold up on the Mistral MetaMath finetune. Gemma: R2 0.97 to -10.27, loss delta 0.51 to 4.21, cosine 0.67. Mistral: loss delta 0.15 to 0.16, cosine 0.96.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features and residual representations persist through finetuning to a degree that depends on the model and finetune.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-feature activation similarity of the same base SAE is 0.39 for Gemma (about 10% of features above 0.8) and 0.958 for Mistral. Logit similarity is high in both, but the authors attribute this mostly to the unchanged unembedding.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual SAE features can persist after finetuning even when the SAE's overall reconstruction fails.

record.peer_reviewed: Alignment Forum post; peer review not stated
record.problems: Only two model/finetune pairs and one residual layer per model are studied. The finetunes differ in provenance, including the extra instruct-model step for Gemma. The experiments use the base SAE training distributions, not finetune-specific or out-of-distribution inputs. SAE feature interpretation is not rigorously checked; the authors did not manually verify the Gemma features. They report numerical instability in reconstruction loss and variance explained and filter outliers for those experiments. Uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted to meet the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: All: no scale sweep and no independently trained models.
No mapping between independently trained models; only reuse of a base SAE on a finetune.
Features are not learned independently in each model and then matched.
No variation of the similarity measure or inputs across converging models.
No test of partial convergence or its causes across independent models.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4/V6/V7 links and labels should be dropped. A base model and its own finetune are not independently trained models, so these results concern representation stability under finetuning, not convergence. The single residual layer, the extra instruct step for Gemma, and the in-distribution data are further limits.

versions.untested_parts: No size or capability sweep, nor comparison across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives or data.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.
No different initialization seeds or shared-subspace analysis across seed-trained networks.

Tests reuse of a base-trained SAE on a related finetuned model, not explicit linear maps between independently trained representations, stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired data.
Does not compare independently trained SAE features or test recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across different models.
Does not vary neighbour count or other similarity settings, and does not test out-of-distribution inputs. Its inputs are the original SAE training datasets.
Shows transfer differs between two model pairs, but does not establish whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain alignment; no plateau is tested.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The reused SAE retains similar feature densities and high feature activation similarity, with only a small reconstruction-loss delta; see r15-r20, r22, r24, r32-r35.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The reused SAE has much worse reconstruction on the finetune, including a negative variance-explained score; low mean activation similarity also indicates incomplete transfer, though some features remain similar. See r9-r14, r21, r25-r31.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: For Gemma, mean activation similarity is 0.39 while mean logit similarity is 0.952; the authors caution that the latter is inflated by the relatively unchanged unembedding matrix, illustrating that transfer conclusions depend on the operational measure. See r25-r27.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Several SAE reconstruction measures deteriorate substantially, indicating incomplete transfer for this pair. See r9-r14 and r25.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: This pair has high residual and feature similarity and a near-unchanged loss delta, so the poor-transfer result does not hold across both tested pairs. See r2, r15-r20, r22, r32-r35.
